source.label: mtg-jp.com coverage, 2023 Asia Vintage Championship トップ8デッキリスト

notes.text: Held inside Players Convention Aichi 2023, organized by BIG MAGIC. mtg-jp prints card names in Japanese (Power, duals and other old cards in English); `name` is the English name, checked against Scryfall, and `printed_as` the Japanese as printed. Archetypes are translated from mtg-jp's Japanese labels; English player names are from Melee. Every list matches mtgtop8's copy of the Melee lists card for card (except mtgtop8's spelling "Lorien Revealed").

Placings are mtg-jp's (Winner, Runner-up, Top 4, Top 8), confirmed by the playoff matches on the Melee page, entered there after the event: quarterfinals Hirasawa def. Marumo 2-1, Hayasaki def. Shinohara 2-0, Yamamoto def. Ota 2-0, Takei def. Hosomi 2-0; semifinals Hirasawa def. Hayasaki 2-0, Yamamoto def. Takei 2-1; final Hirasawa def. Yamamoto 2-1. mtgtop8, MTGGoldfish and Melee's own final standings all order the Top 8 differently, and wrongly.
mtg-jp dates the event 25-26 November; the Top 8 profiles went up on the 26th.
Seeds are the standings after the last Swiss round (Round 8) on the Melee page; they match the quarterfinal pairings (1v8, 2v7, 3v6, 4v5).
